record.title: Beijing seeks proposals for disruptive AI technology projects
record.summary: A 23 October notice from the Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission and Zhongguancun Administrative Committee solicits reserve projects across three AI technology tracks: inference chips, disruptive algorithms and frontier large-model technology. The chip track seeks an integrated chip/software/model-adaptation solution validated by at least two real user organizations. The algorithm track seeks a new architecture tested at 10,000,000,000 or more parameters against a best same-scale Transformer baseline. A third track targets adaptive or self-improving large-model systems. Beijing had already solicited a non-Transformer architecture at this scale in 2025, and the enterprise 2:1 matching condition also appeared in that call. The new notice adds a two-user chip-validation requirement and a distinct adaptive large-model track. It states research goals and solicitation rules, not awarded funding, built systems or measured technical results.
organizations: Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission and Zhongguancun Administrative Committee published a 23 October call soliciting reserve topics in AI compute chips, disruptive algorithms and frontier large-model technology.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The call's stated chip track seeks an integrated chip, board or system, software and model-adaptation solution, with application validation by at least two real user organizations; its algorithm track seeks a new neural architecture tested at 10,000,000,000 or more parameters against a best same-scale Transformer baseline.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice describes a third track for adaptive or self-improving large-model systems, sets a typical project period of no more than two years, and states an application deadline of 2026-11-02 at 18:00; enterprise applicants must provide matching investment at no less than 2:1 against public science funds.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The solicitation does not state a total program budget or named awardees and provides no evidence that a proposed architecture, chip or model has been built, validated or shown to outperform a baseline.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A separate 2025 Beijing call had already solicited a non-Transformer architecture with a 10-billion-or-more-parameter model and required enterprise applicants to match public science funds at 2:1; this establishes continuity in stated policy mechanisms, not funded work or technical results.

evidence_gaps.description: The notice gives no total grant pool, per-project allocation, selected applicants or award decisions.
No proposed or completed chip, model, architecture, baseline, artifact or measured result is included in the call.

brief.importance_rationale: If selected projects deliver, the call could steer regional R&D toward AI inference chips, non-Transformer architectures and adaptive large-model systems. Beijing already solicited 10-billion-parameter non-Transformer work and a 2:1 enterprise match in 2025; the 2026 notice adds two-user chip validation and a distinct adaptive-model track. It gives no funding pool, awards or outcomes, so the score reflects bounded potential policy consequence rather than achieved technical progress.
limitations: The source establishes a regional solicitation and its stated aims, not project selection, funding, completion or technical progress.
The notice provides no program budget or per-project cap; the 2:1 enterprise matching requirement does not establish actual additional private investment.
The algorithm track names a same-scale Transformer comparison but gives no exact baseline, dataset, metric or test protocol.
The notice is specific to Beijing and should not be generalized to all of China or treated as a national program.
The 2025 comparison establishes that some targets and the enterprise 2:1 matching rule were previously solicited; no 2025 awards, matched-fund delivery or technical results were checked.
organizations: Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission

relationships.summary: Beijing issued a separate Oct 20 call for AI-enabled cybersecurity and adversarial-testing projects. The two notices are distinct regional solicitations by the same agencies and should not be merged.

technical.claimed_result: The commission seeks proposals that could improve inference hardware, non-Transformer architectures or adaptive large models; these are stated objectives, not achieved results.
technical.demonstrated_result: The original Chinese notice establishes the three solicitation tracks, some technical targets and applicant/deadline conditions. It reports no completed system or measured performance.
technical.mechanism: The call solicits development and application validation of an AI-oriented compute-chip stack; a non-Transformer neural architecture co-designed with low-bit quantization; and adaptive large-model methods such as recursive improvement, new attention and native multimodality.
technical.regime: Beijing municipal reserve-topic solicitation dated 23 October 2026. The stated project term is generally no more than two years; chip proposals require validation at two real user organizations, and the architecture track names a 10,000,000,000-parameter minimum for model validation.
technical.strongest_baseline: The call requires a comparison to a best same-scale Transformer for the algorithm track but names no specific baseline, dataset, metric or evaluation protocol. No comparative result is reported.

brief.title: Beijing seeks proposals for disruptive AI technology projects
brief.why_it_matters: The call renews Beijing’s earlier focus on large non-Transformer models and enterprise co-financing while adding real-user validation for chip proposals and a distinct adaptive large-model track. The 2025 notice shows the 10-billion-parameter and 2:1 mechanisms are not new in 2026; this notice still provides a current, specific regional R&D solicitation. Neither notice establishes awards, delivered private capital or technical outcomes.

related.summary: Beijing issued a separate Oct 20 call for AI-enabled cybersecurity and adversarial-testing projects. The two notices are distinct regional solicitations by the same agencies and should not be merged.

other.title: Beijing seeks proposals for AI cyber-defense and adversarial-testing projects
other.summary: On Oct 20, the Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission and Zhongguancun Administrative Committee opened a call for 2026 reserve projects in two areas: AI-enabled cybersecurity products and a high-fidelity adversarial testing and validation platform. The original Chinese notice describes multi-agent security operations, malicious-component detection, attack-surface management and unknown-attack defense as research directions; it calls for automated adversarial testing and high-simulation cyber ranges in the second area. It limits the first topic to enterprise applicants or enterprise-led consortia and the second to universities and research institutes. Each enterprise may submit one project and must provide matching funds at least 2:1 relative to public science funding. The notice sets a project period generally no longer than 1 year and an application window from Oct 20 through Oct 29. It is a solicitation, not evidence of selections, funding totals, deployed systems or measured cybersecurity outcomes.
organizations: Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission
